expectations.name: cross-document-contradiction
expected_behavior: Judges against a model of the whole document, not a sequential read: the report pairs findings whose two halves sit in different sections, and cites both locations for each — a defect only visible once both ends are held at once
Reports the contradiction as a Blocker citing both locations, not just the later one
Flags the twice-repeated browser claim as redundancy
Numbers the findings and groups them Blocker / Should-fix / Nit

expectations.name: flag-dubious-claim
expected_behavior: Fixes grammar, terminology, and clarity directly in the file
Does not silently rewrite the dubious claim — raises it as a question stating what it would expect instead and why
Lists the flagged claim among the items awaiting the user's decision
Invents no replacement fact it cannot ground

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the scope line and then the findings — the scope line is the first fact, not preamble
No narration of what it is about to do, and no step commentary
Each finding stated once; no closing summary re-listing findings already shown
After applying the fixes, states the edit classes and the file path
Does not paste the document back into chat

expectations.name: create-grounded-manual
expected_behavior: Fixes audience, product, and purpose, asking only the gaps it cannot infer — audience, key tasks, terminology — in one batched round
Uses one term per concept from the first line and a task-oriented structure (overview → prerequisites → tasks → reference → troubleshooting), omitting empty sections
Writes the file, states the path, and does not paste the manual back
Names, in the reply, what the whole-document pass changed — the pass leaves no other trace, so an unreported one cannot be told from one that never ran

expectations.name: drift-across-a-set
expected_behavior: Treats the three files as one document and checks consistency across all of them, not file by file
Flags workspace/project as terminology drift, naming both files
Flags the missing Backup section as a completeness gap — a dangling reference, not a wording nit

expectations.name: revise-keeps-the-whole-coherent
expected_behavior: Infers revise mode and moves in document order, one unit at a time, applying only what the user agrees to
Applies the rename to the unit under discussion only, rather than sweeping the document on its own initiative
Runs the coherence check and reports the later occurrences as now-inconsistent, with their locations, before moving on
Sweeps the rest only once the user asks for it, which is the difference between a batch edit and an agreed one
Reports each turn as the proposed change plus the coherence-check result — not a reprint of the document

expectations.name: normalize-to-the-doc-s-own-convention
expected_behavior: Normalizes to the variety the document predominantly uses, fixing the minority outliers rather than converting the whole document
Reports the mixed spelling in both directions — how many sites use each form and which it took as the document's own — so the reader can overrule the choice without re-reading the document
Reports the mix as a spelling-variety defect either way, since the author may have meant the other one
Re-aligns the table columns and reflows to the doc's own 100-column wrap, not an imposed house default
States edit classes and counts without pasting the document back
